posts.text:
BREAKING: China purchased +25 tonnes of gold in August via the London OTC market, according to Goldman Sachs estimates.

This is +25% more than the official +20 tonnes reported by China's central bank for this month.

This also follows estimated purchases of +35, +40, and +48 tonnes in July, June, and May, respectively.

Over these 4 months, China's estimated gold purchases through the OTC market exceeded officially reported purchases by 83 tonnes, or +128%.

Meanwhile, global central banks are estimated to have acquired +79 tonnes of gold in August, +365% above the pre-2022 average of +17 tonnes.

China is stockpiling gold.

BREAKING: The Strategic Petroleum Reserve (SPR) fell -300,000 barrels last week, to 282.7 million barrels, the lowest level since October 1982.

Since March 20th, US oil inventories in the SPR have dropped -132.8 million, or -32%.

We have now seen drawdowns in 29 of the last 30 weeks.

For perspective, oil reserves in the SPR stood at 653.9 million barrels in 2020, or +131% above current levels.

Meanwhile, commercial crude oil stocks excluding the SPR dropped -3.1 million barrels last week, to 412.5 million barrels, the lowest reading since the end of July.

This is also ~3% below the 5-year average for this time of year.
